glosses: to speed up, to hasten transitive
разг. то же, что ускорять [1]; делать более быстрым, увеличивать скорость
To cause to move faster; to quicken the motion of; to add to the speed of.
To quicken the natural or ordinary progression or process of.

examples.text: to accelerate the growth of a plant, the increase of wealth, etc.
The company plans to accelerate its growth with new marketing strategies.
She had to accelerate her work pace to meet the deadline.

Nevertheless, it is clear that the global energy demand for air-conditioning will grow substantially as nations become more affluent, with the consequences of climate change potentially accelerating the demand.

glosses: To cause a change of velocity.
To hasten, as the occurrence of an event.

examples.text: to accelerate our departure

glosses: To enable a student to finish a course of study in less than normal time.
To become faster; to begin to move more quickly.

examples.text: The car began to accelerate as soon as the light turned green.

glosses: Grow; increase.
Accelerated; quickened; hastened; hurried.

examples.text: ... a general knowledg of the definition of motion, and of the distinction of natural and violent, even and accelerate, and the like, sufficing.

glosses: To accelerate; to increase speed.

examples.text: The car sped up as it went around the corner.

glosses: To accelerate (something): to increase its speed, to make it go faster.

examples.text: More fast trains between England and Scotland, and additional "car-sleeper" overnight services for motorists, are important features of British Railways summer timetables, which come into operation on June 17. In all, 98 long-distance trains will be speeded-up to save 10-75 min. and many will make non-stop runs at an average speed of 60 m.p.h. or more.
You shouldn't speed up your car when you go around corners.
The through Moorgate service has been most handsomely speeded up, and suburban trains in both directions now run non-stop between Kings Cross (Underground) and Elstree.
Work on anti-frost precautions on diesel locomotives is to be speeded up to ensure that most if not all locomotives have been dealt with before the winter sets in.

glosses: To move or act in a quick fashion.
To make someone speed up or make something happen quicker.

examples.text: I would hasten my escape from the windy storm.

Hamlet:
Bid the players make haste.
Will you two help to hasten them?
A dearth of signalmen and the high cost of labour is hastening an elimination process that already was well under way before the second world war.

glosses: To cause some scheduled event to happen earlier.

examples.text: The decision to hasten completion of the electrification of London Midland Region main lines from Euston to the north and the subsequent diversion of some traffic to the Western Region in order to allow the engineers fuller track occupation, have focused attention on the two main routes between London, Birmingham and Wolverhampton.
[…]and prescribed policies and packages of military, economic and technical assistance to hasten their inevitable march toward development and modernity.

glosses: Aumentar la velocidad.

examples.text: España aceleró el crecimiento de su PIB, redujo la deuda pública, redujo la tasa de desempleo del 23% al 15% en 3 años y redujo la inflación por debajo del 3%.
